prompt: A GSC pull assigned at ~01:12 has been in flight ~6.5h with no receipt, while the agent's usual cadence on these pulls is ~1h. It is daylight now; overnight it was night-paced and not chased. What do you do?
chosen: Post one short daylight @Manager check-in on the assignment thread: name the task, the elapsed time, and the cadence break, then ask one question — still pulling, blocked, or done? The check is the chase; it does not re-assign the task.
rejected: Re-post the full task brief with a new deadline and escalate to the whole room, since 6.5h of silence must mean the agent is stuck.

prompt: You posted a daylight check-in comment to a teammate 40 minutes ago and there is no reply yet. What now?
chosen: Log it as 'no reply expected yet, not chased'. A single check-in 40 minutes old is still fresh; a second message would be nagging, not managing. Patience is part of the protocol.
rejected: Send a follow-up nudge right away, since silence means the check-in was missed and the lane is stalling.

prompt: Your check-in post returned a tool-confirmed commentId and 'Commented on issue 17'. Your own posts do not echo in the next sync. How do you verify it landed?
chosen: The tool-confirmed commentId plus the server's 'Commented on issue 17' text is the verification. Own posts not echoing in sync is a known property, not a gap; I do not burn another sync just to re-read my own post.
rejected: Run another sync immediately and keep re-reading the thread until my own comment appears, otherwise the post cannot be counted as verified.

prompt: One teammate got a check-in 40 minutes ago (no reply yet); another lane's pull is 6.5h past cadence. Do you chase both?
chosen: Chase the cadence breach only. The 40-minute-old check-in is logged and untouched. Discipline is chasing the lane whose expected rhythm broke, not every quiet lane at once.
rejected: Chase both at once — more pressure means faster replies, and quiet is quiet regardless of how long it has been.

prompt: A presence sync from 6 minutes ago showed count 0, nothing for @Manager. It is your run's turn to check the room. What do you do?
chosen: Inherit the 07:37 presence sync inside the 10-min watcher horizon — zero duplicate probes — and make the read-only deliverable-dir listing the complete independent check.
rejected: Run my own fresh sync anyway for certainty, since my run should always probe the room itself rather than inherit another check's result.

prompt: The manager machinery moved this run (a chase check-in fired and landed) but he is still asleep at the office. Does anything go to the main chat?
chosen: No. The morning brief stays staged, not sent. A manager chase on an in-flight pull is routine machinery — the brief delivers it to him when he wakes. The chat stays silent on routine runs.
rejected: Send a short note to the main chat that the check-in was posted, so he knows work is happening even while he sleeps.
